title: Test forms are Lipschitz in the Euclidean coefficient norm
statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k: a C^∞ k-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). For a k-covector β write |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β, the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15. Then there is a real number c ≥ 0 such that |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c·dist(x, y) for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P.
lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ x y : Euclid P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y) ≤ c * dist x y
